solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Crow over tucking into spread cool dad cooked

indicators.note: tucking into says the first piece is pushed inside the jumbled letters that follow
spread means these letters are laid out in a fresh order

parts.note: O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A cockerel crowing about a cool father who has made a spread of food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' looks like the meal, but it rearranges COOL DAD COOKED; 'tucking into' puts O inside that jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: The cockerel's morning cry is written as this noise, so it names a rooster's crow.

clue.text: Vegetable's said to be burned

indicators.note: said tells us the word is heard rather than read, giving a near-identical spoken form

parts.note: chard is a leafy vegetable; the possessive gives chard's

explanation.surface: A vegetable is reputed to have been burnt in the cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' makes the possessive chard's sound like a past participle.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scorched black by fire is charred, a direct synonym of burnt.

clue.text: Member meets unknown host

parts.note: an arm is a limb, a member of the body
Y is one of the algebraic unknowns, x, y and z

explanation.surface: A club member is introduced to a stranger who is hosting the evening.
explanation.definitionFit: Host in the old sense of a multitude, especially an armed force, as in the heavenly host.

clue.text: Old money around centre of Hull creates wealth

indicators.note: around says the first pieces surround what comes next

parts.note: pence are British coins, money

indicators.note: centre of picks the two middle letters of the word Hull

explanation.surface: Inherited cash from the middle of Hull, a northern English port city, makes someone rich.
explanation.walkthrough: Hull is a city in Yorkshire, England; 'centre of' takes just its middle pair, and 'around' wraps the old money round them.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulence is great riches or luxurious abundance, a synonym for wealth.

clue.text: Flower planted in pail hadn't pushed up

indicators.note: pushed up says the hidden letters are read backwards
planted in says the flower is buried inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A flower that was planted in a bucket failed to come up.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Flower planted' as the definition, but 'planted in' is what signals the letters hidden in 'pail hadn't'; 'pushed up' then turns them round in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The dahlia is a showy garden bloom grown from tubers, an example of a flower.

clue.text: English queen's introduced to not yell when broadcast but speak thus?

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the way to speak; the answer is the adverb that tells how

indicators.note: introduced to says the abbreviation is placed inside the scrambled words
broadcast means scattered about, so the letters of not yell are rearranged

parts.note: Qu. is a dictionary abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: An English queen is advised not to shout when on air, but to talk with fine fluency.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen here is not the usual R or ER but the dictionary abbreviation Qu.; 'introduced to' sets it inside the 'when broadcast' jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak fluently and persuasively, without yelling, is to talk in an articulate manner.

clue.text: After month ten birds will appear in groups of eight

indicators.note: after says the birds come following the month in the build

parts.note: October is the tenth month, abbreviated Oct
Aves is the scientific class name for birds

explanation.surface: After October, ten birds turn up in flocks of eight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ten' looks like a number of birds, but it belongs with 'month' to name October.
explanation.definitionFit: In music and verse an octave is a set of eight notes or lines, so these are eights.

clue.text: Cowards upset as cadets cry

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so these letters are tipped into a new order

explanation.surface: Upset military trainees burst into tears and are called chickens.
explanation.definitionFit: A playground term for timid people who are easily frightened, a synonym for cowards.

clue.text: Criticise poor speaker

parts.note: poor quality is bad
the mouth is the organ that speaks

explanation.surface: Someone finds fault with a weak public orator.
explanation.definitionFit: To bad-mouth someone is to speak ill of them, an informal synonym for criticise.

clue.text: Alcohol measure for your eyes only?

definitions.meaning: the upside-down bottle dispenser in a British pub that pours a fixed shot of spirits
relating to the eye or vision, as in the nerve that serves sight

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a pub spirit-dispensing gauge and anything to do with sight, the eye's sense.

clue.text: Board attack after French art forms annoy you

indicators.note: after says the attack comes following the French word

parts.note: to board a bus is to get on it
es is French for 'art' as in thou art (tu es)
to go at someone is to attack them

explanation.surface: A board's offensive against French art movements gets on your nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French art' is not painting: it is the verb 'art' (you are), which in French is ES.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning to irritate someone thoroughly, so it stands for annoying a person.

clue.text: Kangaroo's ready

definitions.meaning: the wallaroo, a large Australian marsupial of the kangaroo family
slang for cash, as in ready money; this is one European currency

explanation.definitionFit: One word names both an Australian marsupial and the single currency of much of Europe.

clue.text: Note marquee is ramshackle with volume restricted

indicators.note: restricted says the jumble hems in the next letter
ramshackle means tumbledown and disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A notice says the tumbledown tent has limited capacity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restricted' puts V inside the 'ramshackle' jumble of MARQUEE IS.
explanation.definitionFit: A semiquaver is a sixteenth note in music, an example of a note.

clue.text: A meal began to go wrong. That can be handled

indicators.note: going wrong means the letters break down into a new order

explanation.surface: A dinner started to fail, but the problem can be dealt with.
explanation.definitionFit: Something capable of being controlled or coped with is easy to deal with.

clue.text: Soldiers step around new munitions

parts.note: OR, other ranks, is the usual abbreviation for ordinary soldiers

indicators.note: around says the first pieces enclose the next letter

parts.note: a step is a dance, as in a dance step

explanation.surface: Troops march around fresh weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Military supplies such as artillery and ammunition, the same as munitions.

clue.text: Posh North American journalist's left idle

parts.note: U means upper-class, posh, in British usage
ED, editor, is the crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A smart North American reporter has been left with nothing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left idle has not been put to any use.

clue.text: Grant is cast about right in leading role

indicators.note: about says the jumble goes around the next letter
cast means thrown about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Cary Grant is cast in a film as the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like film casting, but it jumbles GRANT IS; 'about' wraps that round R.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor billed at the top plays the main part, featured as the star.

clue.text: Observation — I will be trapped by error, getting knocked back

indicators.note: knocked back means sent backwards, so the result is read in reverse
trapped by says the letter is caught inside the word for error

parts.note: a lapse is a slip or error

explanation.surface: A remark about how I will be caught out by a mistake and rebuffed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trapped by' puts I in LAPSE to make LAIPSE; 'getting knocked back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Espial is an old word for spying or watching closely, so it means an act of seeing.

clue.text: For now spoken name could be he, she or it

definitions.text: could be he, she or it

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: spoken says the word is to be heard, giving a spelling that sounds the same

parts.note: the word now said aloud

explanation.surface: For the moment, a spoken name might be a man, a woman or a thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'now spoken' gives the sound NOU, so the middle reads NOUN, the very thing a name is.
explanation.definitionFit: He, she and it are words standing in place of nouns, so each is an example.

clue.text: Vigorous London soccer team having axed Bobby or Jack?

indicators.note: having axed says a part of the team's name is cut away

parts.note: Charlton Athletic is a football club in south-east London
Bobby and Jack Charlton were the brothers in England's 1966 World Cup-winning team

explanation.surface: A lively London football club has sacked a famous player.
explanation.walkthrough: CHARLTON ATHLETIC is a London football club; Bobby and Jack Charlton were English footballing brothers.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sporty and fit is strong and energetic, so the adjective means vigorous.

clue.text: Internally shortens or straightens muscles

indicators.note: internally says the answer lies within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Something inside shortens or straightens the muscles.
explanation.definitionFit: Tensors are muscles that tighten or stretch a body part, an example of muscles.

clue.text: Angler's delight at the end of the day is surprisingly fluent

definitions.text: Angler's delight at the end of the day

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests an unexpected order, so the letters of fluent are rearranged

explanation.surface: A happy fisherman, after a day at the river, speaks with unexpected ease.
explanation.definitionFit: A full catch in the landing net is what a fisherman hopes to see by evening.

clue.text: With injection of oxygen, grey and sober could be something fruity!

indicators.note: an injection puts something in, so the next letter goes inside the jumble
could be says these letters might become something else when rearranged

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A dull, staid person given a shot of oxygen turns lively.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface paints a dreary person, but 'and' only joins the two fodder words that 'could be' rearranges; 'With injection of' adds the oxygen.
explanation.definitionFit: A gooseberry is a tart green berry, an example of a fruit.

clue.text: Insect bite returns

indicators.note: returns says the word goes back the other way

parts.note: a sharp tang or bite of flavour

explanation.surface: An insect's sting keeps coming back.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnat is a small two-winged fly, an example of an insect.

clue.text: Coming over, one that's seen in bar in college

indicators.note: coming over says the word is turned upside down in this down entry

parts.note: a musical note appears within a bar of a score

explanation.surface: Someone coming over is spotted in a pub near the college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub, but it is a bar of music. ETON is a famous English public school, formally Eton College.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton College, near Windsor in England, is the elite fee-paying school usually just called by its town.

clue.text: Male wearing a short haircut becomes explosive

indicators.note: wearing says the following pieces go round the letter like clothing

parts.note: a bob is a short hairstyle cut level around the head

explanation.surface: A man sporting a cropped hairstyle turns volatile.
explanation.definitionFit: The atomic bomb is the archetypal nuclear explosive device.

clue.text: Lie about king creates disagreement

indicators.note: about says the first word goes around the next letter

parts.note: fiction is an invented story, a lie
R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: A falsehood about the monarch causes a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Friction is conflict or tension between people, a synonym for disagreement.

clue.text: International tangle? Listen, I straightened out this clever set

indicators.note: straightened out means put into order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An international mix-up? Listen, I sorted it out for the brainy crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tangle' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder; 'straightened out' rearranges TANGLE LISTEN I after the single I.
explanation.definitionFit: The intelligentsia are the intellectual elite of a society, a learned class.
